$comment: Pinned expected-case denominators for every devnet-validate suite.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (#953, same class as #945/#923): every suite in this
harness reports N/N by counting the rows it produced. A stimulus that never
fires produces no row, so N/N is tautological — '26/26 adversarial' said
nothing about whether 26 cases ran. A denominator is only meaningful when it
comes from OUTSIDE the run that produces the numerator.
Every count here is checked in two directions:
hard-fails below it, and records status='short' in the JSON).
2. scripts/test-denominators.sh asserts these counts still match the
scripts on disk, so adding a script without bumping the pin fails CI-
style verification rather than silently widening the gate.
Bump a number here only together with on-disk evidence of the new count.

cli_parity.$comment: One row per tx-zoo/09-cli-parity/09*.sh. EQUAL+DIVERGENT+SKIP+ERROR must sum to this. Env-skips are counted as their own class and never folded into EQUAL.

n2n_adversarial.$comment: Rows in n2n-trace.csv. NOT the same as the count of adv_record call sites (28) — two sites are mutually-exclusive branches. Confirmed live: see the closing evidence on #953.

chaos._comment: expected_scripts = scenario .sh files on disk (excluding lib.sh/run.sh). expected_cases_* = terminal ROWS a given preset produces, which is preset-dependent: the STANDARD set runs 4 scenarios for 5 rows; EXTENDED adds network-partition + disk-full for 6. Pinning a single `expected_cases: 6` from the extended set made every standard run fail gate integrity with 'chaos recorded 5 rows, below the pinned 6' — a denominator no standard run could ever satisfy. ENV-SKIP is a counted class, never silence (#959).

parity_matrix.$comment: The bidirectional accept/reject oracle. Per-invocation totals live in parity-matrix.meta.json (written by bidirectional-parity.sh); this block pins which categories the STANDARD gate must cover, so a run that quietly narrows its category list fails the gate. Before #954 the invocation was a hardcoded 4 categories and the release notes reported '41/41' without ever stating that the zoo has 85 scripts.

excluded_categories.10-gov-lifecycle: Chain-global governance lifecycle: propose -> 3-role vote -> assert enactment. Two batches would create two proposals in the same lane and both vote; ratification is a property of the whole chain, not of a batch, so the second batch's enactment assertion is not independent. Covered on path B only.
excluded_categories.12-post-enactment: Only meaningful once a governance action has actually ENACTED, so it depends on 10 having run and on global chain state. Same reason as 10.
excluded_categories.13-script-purposes: The guarding scripts are fixed (always-true/false V3, one native), so their hashes are deterministic and BOTH parity batches would share one stake credential and one DRep credential. Batch 1 registers and then deregisters it, so batch 2 acts on state batch 1 already mutated — the same class as 05g/05h. These scripts instead demand Haskell confirmation directly: they use wait_all_strict, which requires all three observers and never soft-passes on 'cbp lagging'.
excluded_categories.14-gov-negatives: Governance negatives assert rejection CLASSES against chain-global gov state (live actions, registered DReps). Both batches would target the same actions, so batch 2's result depends on what batch 1 did — same class as 10/12. The rejection class is already compared against cardano-node directly by each script.
excluded_categories.15-asset-lattice: Mint policies are derived from the batch's own payment key, so the two parity batches mint under DIFFERENT policy ids and the resulting values are not comparable cell-for-cell. The properties under test (encodeMap definite/indefinite boundaries at 23/24/256, multi-policy values, mint+burn) are wire-shape properties already checked against cardano-node by zoo_wait_all_observers on every script.

excluded_scripts.05g-cc-hot-key-authorization: Constitutional committee is seated at genesis and is devnet-global. Batch 1 resigns cc-1, so batch 2 correctly receives ConwayCommitteeHasPreviouslyResigned. Giving batch 2 its own committee requires an UpdateCommittee governance action (2+ epoch boundaries). Verified live 2026-08-02, not a dugite defect.
excluded_scripts.05h-cc-resign: Same: a cold-key resignation is one-shot per member and only cc-1/cc-2 are seated.

known_reject_reason_differences.08f-double-spend: #925 - a Conway duplicate input fails at the CBOR set layer. Haskell drops the connection ('mux: bearer closed'); dugite deliberately answers a structured MsgRejectTx naming the rule. dugite is more informative here; not a defect.

rpc._comment: Rows written by rpc/run.sh: 1 service-discovery + 8 service-present + 1 relay-reachable + 2 read-params + 2 cost-models + 2 read-tip + 2 read-utxos + 2 submit-tx + 2 malformed-cbor + 1 oversized + 1 empty-tx + 1 garbage-txoref + 1 duplicate-concurrent-submit + 1 mempool-hygiene = 27. Pinned from OUTSIDE the run so 27/27 is not tautological; a suite that silently stops emitting rows fails the gate instead of reporting a smaller clean sweep.
